purpose: Summative performance task artifact for the unit. Phases 1–3 (Plan, Build, Translate) generate the visible evidence for the rubric across A7.1–A7.4. Phase 4 (Lead) is observational and is captured on the rubric, not on the worksheet.
student_learning_goal: I can plan a parade pattern, lead it, and explain the core to a friend.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can plan a parade pattern, lead it, and explain the core to a friend.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner of the header, holding a small Junior Pattern Conductor certificate, smiling broadly. Slightly larger than other worksheets (~2in tall) to mark this as the summative. References the shared 'Coco the Conductor' asset from blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Plan your core. Draw or sticker the animals that will repeat. Pick 2, 3, or 4 animals. Then circle your core with a loop.
parts.visual_layout: A bordered rectangular box labelled 'My Core' at the top of the page, approximately 4in wide × 1.5in tall — large enough for a child to draw or sticker 2–4 animal icons. To the right of the box, a small Loop Frame icon with the caption 'Don't forget to circle your core!' as a reminder. Below the box, a thin horizontal four-animal reference key (Bea, Finn, Bibi, Moss).

parts.answer_key: Open-ended. A response is correct if (a) the My Core box contains 2, 3, or 4 distinct animals, (b) those animals form a recognisable repeating unit (the AB / ABC / ABB / etc. structure should be clear from the order), and (c) a closed loop or circle is drawn around the core. This part scores A7.2 on the summative rubric.

parts.student_instructions: Build your parade. Fill ALL 8 cells. Make sure your core repeats AND your parade extends both ways.
parts.visual_layout: A long horizontal parade strip with 8 cells, all empty (light-grey solid outlines). The strip is wider than the My Core box above so the child has room to repeat their core multiple times. A left-arrow on the outside of cell 1 reads 'before the start' and a right-arrow on the outside of cell 8 reads 'after the end' — visual cues that the parade extends in both directions.

parts.answer_key: Open-ended. A response is correct if (a) the 8-cell sequence is a valid repetition of the child's chosen core from Part 1, (b) the core repeats consistently across all 8 cells (i.e., the parade extends correctly in both directions). This part scores A7.1 (creates a pattern) and A7.4 (extends in both directions) on the summative rubric.

parts.student_instructions: Show your SAME core a different way. Pick sounds or bodies. Fill in the parade. Then finish the sentence at the bottom.
parts.visual_layout: A second 8-cell parade strip, identical in size to Part 2's, all cells empty. Below the strip, a caption box reads 'My core was the same. I just used ___ instead of animals.' with a wide line for the child to write or draw what they used (e.g., 'sounds', 'bodies', 'claps and stomps'). At the bottom, a combined reference key showing sound icons (clap, stomp, hum, tap) and body icons (tall, small, jump, freeze).

parts.answer_key: Open-ended. A response is correct if (a) the 8-cell strip uses a non-animal representation (sounds OR body icons), (b) the structural core is the same as the child's Part 1 / Part 2 core, (c) the strip extends in both directions consistently, and (d) the caption sentence is filled with a description of what they used (e.g., 'sounds', 'bodies'). This part scores A7.3 on the summative rubric.

early_finisher_prompt: Show your parade to a friend! Ask them: 'What is my core? What comes after my last animal? What came before my first animal?'
teacher_notes: This is the SUMMATIVE artifact. Score against the rubric using these mappings: A7.1 = is Part 2 a valid repeating pattern? A7.2 = is the core in Part 1 correctly identified and looped? A7.3 = does Part 3 use the same structural core as Part 2? A7.4 = does Part 2 extend correctly in both directions (cells 1, 2 backward and cells 7, 8 forward)? Conference observations from the lesson's Phase 4 (Lead) round out the rubric for any cell where the worksheet evidence is unclear. Hand back with the Junior Pattern Conductor certificate as part of the closing ceremony.
